name: AZ-DustBench
description: AZ-DustBench is a station-level benchmark for minute-scale prediction of dust visibility collapse at Arizona weather stations, covering 2005 to 2025, with event-based splits, per-threshold survival labels, and a frozen seven-rung baseline ladder anchored on a gradient-boosted station champion. The release adds two training-free feature extractors, cubical persistent homology of the lowest-tilt radar reflectivity field and a wind-conditioned graph-scattering transform on the station network, together with the paired-increment harness that measures their gain over the station champion. It ships the deciding analyses behind the accompanying article: the radar-versus-satellite sensor ablation, the full-strength-reference ablation, the rerun raw-field control, the four-column field arm, and the leave-one-year-out and nested out-of-selection generalization checks.
